thread.title: Cyclical, IPO Stocks Enjoy Gains, Apple Exhales; 5 Sectors Are Jamming

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Cyclical, IPO Stocks Enjoy Gains, Apple Exhales; 5 Sectors Are Jamming

organizations.name: sectors are jamming tabula rasa healthcare

text:
Tabula Rasa Healthcare ( TRHC ), DocuSign ( DOCU ), Atlassian ( TEAM ) and Funko ( FNKO ) helped lead a chorus of solid gains among new IPO stocks, while cyclicals also helped sustain a decent day in stocks today. (See the statistics and charts on these and other new-issue leaders in the IPO Leaders stock list .)
X Strength in software, consumer, medical, retail and business services stocks continue to provide a sturdy backbone for the 3,452-day-long bull run, which according to Reuters is poised to become the longest bull market in history on Wednesday. In fact, these five sectors take the top 5 rankings within IBD's sector-oriented stock research tables .
The gains by these five sectors , which include fistfuls of big market winners, range from 19.9% since Jan. 1 (Retail) to 29.5% (Software) through Monday's market close. They represent the new innovative companies that are helping grow the economy, boost worker productivity and improve the quality of life.
The Nasdaq composite led with a gain of 0.5%. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average rose 0.2% to 0.3%, the Russell 2000 rallied 1.1%. Volume grew on both exchanges, according to early data.
Within the 30-stock Dow Jones industrials, Boeing ( BA ), Caterpillar ( CAT ), Home Depot ( HD ) and Goldman Sachs ( GS ) paced the upside. Fellow component JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) gained 0.6% after the bank announced a plan to take market share from investing websites and apps with a free trading offer on its own mobile app.
The Wall Street titan edged closer to a 118.39 buy point in a long saucer with handle .
Dairy, meat, tobacco, soap and confectionery shares all fell. In contrast, homebuilding stocks showed some badly needed pep. Toll Bros . ( TOL ) gapped up more than 13% and reached as high as 39.80, erasing more than two months' worth of losses.
The luxury homebuilder notched a 27% increase in revenue to $1.91 billion in the July-ended fiscal third quarter. That's on top of an 18% gain in the year-ago period. It also shows acceleration over a 17% year-over-year increase in fiscal Q2 (ended in April).
Horsham, Pa.-based Toll is still in base-building mode .
Among IPO Stocks DocuSign cleared a 62.25 buy point in a nine-week cup with handle. Volume started out strong, but then quieted down to end roughly 15% below its 50-day average of 1.56 million shares.
The specialist in e-signature technology in enterprise software markets earned a penny a share in the April-ended fiscal first quarter as revenue jumped 37% to $155.8 million, a record for quarterly total sales.
In a recent IBD Weekly story on IPO stocks , DocuSign qualified as one of 37 firms that have gained 30% or more since their 2018 debuts.
Spotify ( SPOT ) halted a two-day slump, rising more than 2%. At 190.38, the online music streaming giant has shown positive action with rebounds off the 10-week moving average in recent months. Spotify debuted on the NYSE on April 3, ending the session at 149.01.
Top Tech Stocks Today Apple ( AAPL ) lagged the general market, down 14 cents to 215.32. But the iPhone, cellular-enabled wearables and digital services giant is simply taking a well-needed break after recently marking brand-new all-time highs. On Monday, shares lifted to as high as 219.18, up 18.4% since July 1.
In contrast, the Dow Jones industrial average has gained 6.5% over the same time frame.
Apple has now risen 85% since its first-stage breakout from a cup with handle back on Jan. 6, 2017. That base formed in the midst of an earnings and sales turnaround for Apple, and that base was also a bottoming base .
Please read this recent Stock Market Today column on the reasons why a future $1.25 trillion market value for Apple is not out of the question.
Paycom Software ( PAYC ), a member of Leaderboard since early August, rolled 1.7% higher for a fourth straight gain and a new all-time high.
Keurig Dr Pepper ( KDP ) fell more than 1.5% to 22.99 in super-dull turnover. Despite falling five weeks in a row, the beverage titan still trades above the key 50-day moving average and has a sparkling 47% gain since Jan. 1.
Please read this new column in The Income Investor to learn more about how Keurig Dr Pepper is shaking up the world of dividend stocks.
In Other Financial Markets Energy prices firmed up some more. West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures rallied more than 1.3% to $67.35 a barrel and hit a session high of $68.10. At the session's high, oil has now refueled its year-to-date gain to 12.7%. Gold edged up 0.4% to $1,199.30 a troy ounce and briefly rebounded to the $1,200 level.
The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury bond edged up to 2.84%.
